title: Why Airplane Windows Are Round #shorts
description: Square windows once tore airplanes apart. Here's the deadly lesson behind the round window.

segments.text: Why are airplane windows always round? The answer cost lives.
In 1952, the de Havilland Comet became the world's first jet airliner. It had large, square windows.
Within two years, two Comets broke apart in mid air.
Engineers discovered why. Stress piles up at sharp corners. Every flight, the cabin is pressurized and then released.
Over time, tiny cracks grew from the square corners until the metal tore open.
A round shape spreads that stress evenly, so no single point takes all the force.
So next time you look out a plane window, remember: that curve is keeping you alive. Follow for more.
